newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Report shows Australian charter aircraft old.
newsitem.headline: Report shows Australian charter aircraft old.

text.p: The majority of aircraft in Australia's general aviation sector were considered old with manufacturing dates varying between 1965 and 1980, an aviation report released on Thursday has found.

The report, compiled by the Department of Transport, the Civil Aviation Safety Authority and the Bureau of Air Safety Investigation, said this compared with aircraft owned by the major airlines with most being manufactured since 1980.
It showed regular passenger transport (RPT) activity rose an average 6.3 percent each year in the 10 years from 1986 to 1995.
In the general aviation sector, commercial operations grew an average of only 1.4 percent, charter operations by four percent and flying training by 3.3 percent.
The report said the number of accidents involving Australian fixed-wing aircraft during the last 10 years varied from a low of 171 in 1994 to a high of 214 the year before.
"The number varies from year to year, but shows no upward or downward trend," the report said.
It said the rates of accidents per 100,000 flying hours remained relatively constant for all sectors.
The average accident rate for charter operations was about three times higher than for the low-capacity RPT sector, while the rate for fatal accidents was six times higher.
The report will be updated annually.
